Command: Afflict your souls on the Day of Atonement
Summary: On the tenth day of the seventh month, Israel afflicts its souls — fasting and humbling itself — on the Day of Atonement.
Commandment: On the tenth day of the seventh month, afflict your souls.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The affliction joined the people's repentance to the high priest's atonement in the holy of holies. Debated: some see the commanded observance fulfilled as shadow (Colossians 2:16-17); others keep feasts voluntarily as memorial, not as binding command. The site does not settle whether observance continues.
Purpose: To rehearse God's saving acts at appointed seasons (Leviticus 23); Paul calls Christ our Passover (1 Corinthians 5:7).
